claimsNote: Every flag is literally false. Nothing in this repository implements this contract: the scheduler still executes a barrier node as an ordinary deterministic transform, so a declared IntegratedBarrierPolicy is silently passed today. Flipping any flag to true must be a deliberate, reviewed edit made by the lane that implements the corresponding behavior, never an inference from this corpus.

provenance.note: Every expectation in this corpus is derived only from integrated-barrier-semantics.md and the four frozen schemas. No value is copied from another conformance fixture and no value is imported from a language runtime.

diagnosticEmissionOrder.withinPass: by category in GE1421, GE1422, GE1423, GE1424 order, then node declaration order within each category
diagnosticEmissionOrder.suppression: GE1421 on a node suppresses GE1422 and GE1424 for that node only; it never suppresses GE1423 on that node, any diagnostic on another node, or any later pass

diagnosticBaseLocations.GE1421_INVALID_BARRIER_POLICY: #/nodes/{index}/config + firstInvalidDescendant (config root when the config is not an object)

firstInvalidDescendantRule.order: unknown keys first in ascending Unicode code-point order, then required-or-present fields in contract order, with array elements by increasing index
firstInvalidDescendantRule.note: policyFieldOrder is the declaration order of the IntegratedBarrierPolicy block in integrated-barrier-semantics.md, which differs from the 'properties' order of integrated-barrier-policy.schema.json. The declaration block is the normative contract text and is frozen here.

satisfactionArithmetic.noItems: total == 0 is unsatisfied with reason NO_ITEMS for every kind
satisfactionArithmetic.minimum: minimum > total is MINIMUM_EXCEEDS_TOTAL; otherwise satisfied iff succeeded >= minimum
satisfactionArithmetic.percentage: satisfied iff succeeded * 10000 >= total * basisPoints, both exact safe integers
satisfactionArithmetic.quorum: participants = total - (countAbstainAsParticipant ? 0 : abstained); accepts > participants is QUORUM_EXCEEDS_PARTICIPANTS; otherwise satisfied iff succeeded >= accepts
satisfactionArithmetic.deadlineElapsedRule: deadlineElapsed is true exactly when at least one disposition entry is timed_out

ownership.rule: A barrier config is a claimed policy if and only if it is a portable object carrying exactly this apiVersion value
ownership.unclaimedBehavior: The barrier pass emits no GE1421, GE1422, GE1423 or GE1424 diagnostic for an unclaimed config and does not interpret it; the config keeps whatever pre-contract behavior it already had
ownership.sharedCarrierNote: barrier-vote.schema.json declares the same apiVersion, so the policy and the vote carrier are separated by kind, not by apiVersion. A BarrierVote pasted into a barrier config therefore IS a claimed policy and is diagnosed rather than silently passed.
ownership.unreachableDiagnosticPathsNote: A claimed policy is by definition a portable object carrying the exact apiVersion, so GE1421 can never report at the config root and can never report /apiVersion. Both are unreachable under revision 2.

voteCensus.rule: For a quorum policy, votes is a complete one-record-per-entry census in incoming-edge declaration order, not a list of received ballots
voteCensus.notCastRecordShape: A not-cast record carries sourceNodeId and verdict only. confidenceBasisPoints and evidenceHash are absent, because an entry that cast no ballot supplied neither confidence nor evidence; materializing either would invent a ballot nobody cast.

identifierContract.note: A node identifier is a Graph IR node ID and can never begin with a digit, so a decision document must never accept a node ID the compiler cannot produce. A route key is a SafeRouteId, which may begin with a digit but is never '.' or '..'. The two patterns are deliberately different.

hashContract.canonicalSerializer: canonicalSerialize: UTF-8 JSON with no insignificant whitespace and object keys sorted in ascending Unicode code-point order; arrays keep index order
hashContract.crossRuntimeRequirement: TypeScript and Python MUST each recompute every literal in this corpus from these rules alone; neither may import an expectation from the other

ownershipCases.name: barrier-vote-shaped-config-is-claimed-and-diagnosed
ownershipCases.note: BarrierVote shares the barrier apiVersion with IntegratedBarrierPolicy, so a vote pasted into a barrier config IS a claimed policy and is diagnosed rather than silently passed. 'verdict' is an unknown policy member and unknown keys precede required-or-present fields, so the first invalid descendant is /verdict, not /kind.

ownershipCases.note: a typo inside a claimed carrier is a diagnostic, never a silent pass
